title: Flood Disaster Situation Report (Job ID: job_nepal_2026_case)
executive_summary: Emergency situational report for flood event on unknown (Job: job_nepal_2026_case). AI segmentation estimates 43.8597 km² of inundation (10.1% of AOI). Spatial infrastructure overlay identified an estimated 1055 potentially affected buildings and 97 estimated blocked road segments. Topological network analysis indicates 2 settlements are strictly flood-isolated from their primary administrative towns.

sections.title: 1. Situation Summary
sections.content: Emergency situational report for flood event on unknown (Job: job_nepal_2026_case). AI segmentation estimates 43.8597 km² of inundation (10.1% of AOI). Spatial infrastructure overlay identified an estimated 1055 potentially affected buildings and 97 estimated blocked road segments. Topological network analysis indicates 2 settlements are strictly flood-isolated from their primary administrative towns.

sections.title: 2. Flood Extent
sections.content: Floodwater extents derived by FloodUNet semantic segmentation measure an estimated 43.8597 km² (10.1% of the evaluated Area of Interest), comprising 147 discrete flood regions.
caveats: Water surface area represents model-detected radar backscatter drops; subject to vegetation canopy attenuation.

sections.title: 3. Infrastructure Exposure
sections.content: Spatial intersection analysis identified an estimated 1055 potentially affected buildings (1027 heavily exposed with >=50% overlap), 170 affected road segments (47.348 km of roadway intersected), and 7 potentially affected bridges.
caveats: Spatial overlap represents geodetic exposure, not confirmed structural destruction or collapse.

sections.title: 4. Road Connectivity
sections.content: Topological graph analysis over 10043 road segments identified 97 estimated blocked edges (flood intersection >= 50%) and 224 partially affected edges (< 50%).
caveats: Edges classified as 'estimated_blocked' are impassable in the network model; physical passability requires ground verification.

sections.title: 5. Settlement Isolation
sections.content: Accessibility analysis evaluated settlement reachability to primary administrative centers: 2 settlements are strictly flood-isolated (connected pre-event, severed post-flood); 41 settlements lacked pre-event road connectivity and are NOT attributed to flood impact; 0 connected settlements face vehicular detours.
caveats: Pre-existing network disconnections are strictly excluded from flood isolation statistics.

sections.title: 6. Hospital Accessibility
sections.content: Healthcare network routing determined that 172 settlements retain vehicular access to a hospital, while 2 settlements lost baseline hospital access due to estimated blocked road segments.
caveats: Evaluates road network path reachability only; does not claim hospital operational status, damage, or bed availability.

sections.title: 7. Possible Change/Debris Zones
sections.content: Identified 291 candidate terrain change zones outside primary floodwater extents based on SAR backscatter drops.
caveats: Probabilistic terrain change candidate requiring field validation; not confirmed debris.

sections.title: 8. Data Sources
sections.content:
Satellite Data: European Space Agency (ESA) Copernicus Sentinel-1 SAR and Sentinel-2 MSI via Copernicus Data Space Ecosystem (CDSE).
Infrastructure Baseline: OpenStreetMap pre-event roads, buildings, and bridges.
Training Baseline: Kuro Siwo Benchmark Dataset (NeurIPS 2024 / Orion-AI-Lab).

sections.title: 9. Methodology
sections.content: Pipeline: Pre/Post satellite discovery -> Orbit-matched clipping -> Calibrated decibel radiometric differencing -> FloodUNet 4-stage residual semantic segmentation -> Geodesic polygon extraction -> Spatial exposure overlay against pre-event OSM infrastructure -> NetworkX topological graph routing with Dijkstra shortest-path reachability.

sections.title: 10. Limitations
sections.content:
- All infrastructure exposure estimates are derived from spatial overlays; not confirmed physical damage.
- Road network accessibility uses topological graph models with distance weighting; does not account for real-time traffic or debris velocity.
- Settlements and hospitals reflect pre-event OpenStreetMap metadata without independent population censuses.

sections.title: 11. Validation Notes
sections.content: Copernicus Emergency Management Service activation EMSR927 is strictly reserved as an external post-event validation benchmark and is NOT used as an analysis input. System predictions are independent of published maps.

disclaimer: This report is generated from satellite observations and OpenStreetMap road network models. All damage, inundation, and road blockage statements represent geodetic estimates, not confirmed physical ground truth or structural destruction.
